column1: # OCR-MODELS-2026-10-04: open OCR models on this Mac (M3 Pro, 18 GB), ocr-lab-setup round 1 session 1. PARTIAL:
# chandra-ocr-2-oQ8 and qwen3.5-9b-4bit were refused by the disk rule (deleted weights stay held by hourly
# Time Machine local snapshots, so df did not recover), and teleocr, navidc-ocr, surya-2 need runtimes not yet built.
# Every run went through ops/ocrlab/run-guarded.sh (12 GB, critical pressure, swap +2 GB) via try-mlx.sh, MLX through
# mlx-vlm 0.7.4, greedy decoding. Pages, PDFKit renders at 300 dpi: "ordinary" = Noble_1977 America by design p104
# (602-word transcript), "newspaper" = 1931 Helena Daily Independent p1 (about 5,500 words), whole page and as the
# truth set's 13 overlapping crops (each about 1850x1960 px, sized for Gemini: above several models' input caps,
# e.g. PaddleOCR-VL's 1.0 MP, which is why it reads them badly; ocr-bakeoff should cut smaller crops).
# Peaks are MB, the larger of summed RSS and `footprint` (RSS alone saw 30 MB of a 3 GB MLX array). Seconds are the
# model's read time after load. recall/precision are ROUGH bag-of-words figures against the truth transcript
# (ops/ocrlab/rough-recall.py), a sanity check that a model read the page, NOT ocr-bakeoff's score. Vision on the same
# inputs, from the truth set's own readings: ordinary 0.948/0.979; newspaper whole page 0.223/0.667, crops 0.774/0.720.
# fits = peak under 12 GB, both read to the end, newspaper under 90 s (no candidate meets the 90 s: reading ~5,500 words
# is bound by tokens per second). fits_memory drops the 90 s limit. Three whole-page newspaper runs tripped the swap
# limit with 5-8 GB footprints and the rest looped, so later candidates read only the crops; no model tripped twice
# and nothing crashed. Weights kept: paddleocr-vl-1.6, glm-ocr, hunyuanocr, qwen3.5-2b and -4b, lightonocr (one try left).
